summary: Join our Gender-Based Violence Prevention Strategies Training Course to learn effective methods and tools for creating safer environments for all.
lede: Gender-based violence prevention training helps leaders and practitioners address risks and respond safely to concerns or disclosures. It covers recognizing forms and drivers of GBV, mapping organizational risks, receiving disclosures with care, and strengthening safeguarding policies, reporting channels, and survivor-centered referral pathways. Designed for program managers, safeguarding and protection staff, HR and people managers, and others responsible for safety, the course uses practical scenarios to support prevention and early response without requiring legal or clinical expertise.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who influence safety, behavior, policy, and culture in various settings.
audience: Public sector officials in social services, health
modules: Drivers, Risk Factors, and Contexts of GBV
Legal, Policy, and Ethical Frameworks for GBV Prevention
Recognising Signs and Responding to Disclosures
Referral Pathways, Case Management, and Partnerships
GBV Prevention in Programs and Community Engagement
Workplace GBV, Sexual Harassment, and Organisational Culture
Bystander Intervention and Everyday Prevention Behaviours
Monitoring, Learning, and Sustaining GBV Prevention Efforts
prerequisites: Participants should have a foundational understanding of safeguarding and protection principles. It is recommended to have experience in roles related to program management, HR, social services, or community work.
